description:
BAFU writes some chemical names the way a CAS index does, family first: `Ethane, chloro-` for chloroethane, `Phenol, 2-chloro-` for 2-chlorophenol. For a SimaPro-shaped list the merge already knows how to turn that habit back into the ordinary spelling (#285), and for fourteen BAFU names the ordinary spelling is not merely a synonym of a substance the list holds -- it is the exact name the list publishes for it. The rewriting runs, finds that substance, and then a safety check throws the match away, because the check re-asks its question of the names the row shipped instead of the rewritten name that found the candidate. `Ethane, chloro-` is nobody's preferred name, so the check sees nothing to accept, and the merge mints a second chloroethane -- one with no registry number, which no impact factor can reach. Measured on the 2026-08-20 build of 805e72fd6698 (run 1e4499fbfe55): 24 BAFU rows across these fourteen names, each minting or joining a duplicate of a substance the list already holds under exactly the rewritten name. The issue's other two 16ths, `Benzene, chloro-` and `Benzene, 1,2-dichloro-`, no longer need this route: BAFU ships their registry numbers on sibling rows, and since #309 the vendor's own number is copied across and they match by CAS. The duplicates do double damage now: the minted copy gets a structure from its parseable name, so the list publishes one molecule twice under two identical InChIKeys, and the true substance loses the BAFU spelling from its published synonyms, because a synonym that is some other object's name is stripped -- the copy makes the original harder to find.

The rest of the issue is here too, measured on the build of b03c940bae73 (run 58da3bd39637): 26 more BAFU names, 41 rows, each minting a substance whose InChIKey the list already publishes, and none of them shipping a registry number or an EC number anywhere in BAFU. They needed three different answers, and which one each got turned on whether a *pattern* connected the two spellings. Four are the CAS-index inversion again -- `Ethene, 1,1-dichloro-`, `Toluene, 2-chloro-` -- where the rewriting already produced the right name and the safety check refused it for landing on a synonym rather than on a published name; a name this project derived by de-inverting cannot be the trade name that check exists to stop, so it is now admitted. Four are polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons whose fusion locant BAFU writes in round brackets where the nomenclature uses square ones -- `Benzo(a)anthracene` for benzo[a]anthracene -- which is a habit every list of this lineage carries and so is stated once as a rule. The remaining 18 are pairs of ordinary names for one substance, `Arsine` for hydrogen arsenide and `Methyl Mercaptan` for methanethiol, where there is no pattern to state and the registry number is written on the row instead. Two of those 18 are ties no rule could have broken: `1-Pentanol` reaches both pentan-1-ol and the isomer-unspecified `Pentanol`, and `Nitrogen Monoxide` reaches both nitric oxide and the NOx aggregate, which carry different characterisation factors.

expectations.title: BAFU's four `Ethane, chloro-` rows land on Chloroethane, through the rewritten name
expectations.comment: The named example. Four rows, none carrying a registry number anywhere in BAFU's list, so nothing upstream can supply one and the name route is all there is. `chloroethane` -- the rewriting's output -- is the preferred name of exactly one substance, fo-be8250491b0f9883, CAS 75-00-3, and of nothing else in the published list. On 805e72fd6698 all four rows minted fo-59bb84d3620ba4ea instead: same InChIKey as Chloroethane, no registry number. The basis is claimed so this stays a match made on the derived spelling, visibly, rather than one reached some other way a later change might guess at.

expectations.title: The issue's own example, `3-Methyl-1-butanol`, keeps matching by the vendor's number
expectations.comment: The issue opened with this pair -- an air row shipping 123-51-3 and a water row shipping nothing, the water row minting an empty copy. That healed before this change: #309 copies a number a vendor writes on one row of a name onto its bare siblings, so both rows now match fo-a0b70cd55a7dfe3a by CAS. Claimed here so the healed state is pinned while the rest of the issue is worked, and so the name route accepting more never quietly takes over a row the number already answers for. `Benzene, chloro-` and `Benzene, 1,2-dichloro-` healed the same way.

expectations.title: BAFU's `Nitrogen Monoxide` lands on Nitric oxide, not on the NOx aggregate
expectations.comment: The wider half of #103, and the case that shows why it is curated rather than ruled. No BAFU row of this name ships a number, and the name reaches two substances: `Nitric oxide`, 10102-43-9, the NO molecule, and `Nitrogen Oxides`, 11104-93-1, the NOx aggregate. Those carry different characterisation factors, so a rule that widened the name evidence would have had to guess between them. BAFU ships `Nitrogen Oxides` as a separate row, so this one is the molecule, and `bafu-2026-v1-manual-fixes.json` now says so with the number. Measured on the build of b03c940bae73 (run 58da3bd39637) the row minted fo-0a60f46d4998e148 -- same InChIKey as Nitric oxide, no registry number -- and the published Nitric oxide lost `Nitrogen Monoxide` from its synonyms, stripped for being the copy's name. The basis is claimed as `cas` so this stays a match made on a stated number: if a later change reached the same flow by widening name evidence, that would be a different and weaker answer and this would fail. Selected by the number the fix states rather than by name, and that is #319's lesson in the one shape it did not cover. `subject.name` reads `merge_outcomes.source_name`, which is the row's name *after* harmonisation, not the one the vendor shipped: a row that stops minting a substance of its own and joins an existing one is renamed onto that substance's identity, so BAFU's `Nitrogen monoxide` is recorded as `Nitric oxide` the moment this fix works. A check keyed on the vendor's spelling would then ask about a row that no longer answers to it and report **unresolved** -- passing silently, which is the outcome #319 exists to prevent. The number is what this claim is about, so it is the selector the README asks for.

expectations.title: `Chlorosilane, Trimethyl-` lands on Chlorotrimethylsilane, through a rewritten name that is a synonym
expectations.comment: The named case for the second half of the rule. `Chlorosilane, Trimethyl-` de-inverts to `trimethylchlorosilane`, which this list holds as a ChEBI synonym of `Chlorotrimethylsilane` rather than as its published name -- so the match was found and then refused, because a synonym is not accepted against a substance carrying a registry number. A name this project derived by de-inverting a CAS-index spelling cannot be a trade name or a catalogue code, which is the only thing that refusal exists to stop, so it is now admitted. The rewriting produces `trimethylchlorosilane`; the substance is 75-77-4. Measured on the build of b03c940bae73 (run 58da3bd39637) the rows minted fo-39e77b63b1213afb, with no registry number and so out of reach of every factor. The basis is claimed so this stays a match made on the derived spelling rather than one reached some later change's other way.

expectations.title: BAFU's `Methyl Mercaptan` lands on Methanethiol, through a curated registry number
expectations.comment: The trivial name and the systematic one for CH3SH. BAFU ships no number under this name and no sibling row carries one, so `bafu-2026-v1-manual-fixes.json` states 74-93-1. Measured on the build of b03c940bae73 (run 58da3bd39637) the row minted a numberless copy of a substance the list already publishes. Claimed as `basis=cas` because that is what a stated number should produce; a match reached here by name would mean the fix stopped being applied. Selected by the number the fix states rather than by name, and that is #319's lesson in the one shape it did not cover. `subject.name` reads `merge_outcomes.source_name`, which is the row's name *after* harmonisation, not the one the vendor shipped: a row that stops minting a substance of its own and joins an existing one is renamed onto that substance's identity, so BAFU's `Methyl mercaptan` is recorded as `Methanethiol` the moment this fix works. A check keyed on the vendor's spelling would then ask about a row that no longer answers to it and report **unresolved** -- passing silently, which is the outcome #319 exists to prevent. The number is what this claim is about, so it is the selector the README asks for.

expectations.title: BAFU asks the list to mint no more than 95 new flows
expectations.comment: Measured on the build of b03c940bae73 (run 58da3bd39637) BAFU had 136 rows given a newly minted flow. 41 of them across 26 names were second copies of substances this list already publishes, which is what #103 is; this change places all 41 and nothing else, so the count should reach 95 and stop. The bound is here rather than an equality so that a later change placing more rows is not a failure -- but a change that mints more, or that places these by moving rows nobody named, is.
